newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., budget would raise taxes.
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., budget would raise taxes.

text.p: Florida's Dade County manager has proposed a $4.1 billion budget that raises tax rates for gasoline, water-sewer services and some property owners.

The proposal by County Manager Armando Vidal would raise the county's gasoline tax by one cent, to 11 cents per gallon, to close a budget gap in the county's bus and train system. It restores one of the two cents commissioners cut from that tax last year.

The proposed budget would raise water and sewer rates by 7.5 percent. The water-sewer fee hike is the fourth in four years and is expected to be followed by three more years of increases to pay for court-ordered improvements in the sewer system.
Property tax rates for countywide services, fire-rescue services and libraries would remain the same although many homeowners will pay more because of rising valuations.
The portion of ad valorem taxes that residents of unincorporated areas pay for services only they receive would rise by 45 percent, to $3.20 per $1,000 of assessed value.

Vidal said the tax increases were needed to offset increased spending for police and courts and to make up for a $14 million drop in revenue from Aventura and Pinecrest, which left the county government and incorporated as independent cities.

"We can't allow this government to be put in the position where the city of Miami is today," Vidal told the Miami Herald. "That led us to only one option alone and that is a budget that recommends a tax increase."
City of Miami, Dade's county seat, is under supervision from a state-appointed oversight board because of its failure to eliminate budget deficits.
